new_statements.rule_in_words: No published prose rule was found. Taber's (1993) field-elicited phonetic list marks stress on every polysyllable: 168 of 183 marked polysyllabic tokens have penultimate stress; the residue is 8 final-stressed tokens (the vi-prefixed numerals viɛˈru 'two', viˈti 'seven', viˈaː 'eight', viˈsi 'nine'; aˈwor 'forest'; and vowel-sequence-final iˈtʃei 'this', boloˈdoi 'long', ehɛˈhea 'tail', which are penultimate if the final VV is disyllabic) and 7 antepenultimate tokens, two with a post-tonic schwa (ˈkukəmo 'fingernail', ˈdodəmo 'snake') plus ˈdeweja 'woman', waˈwathono 'sit', teteˈhejeni 'edge', idiˈmoderi 'there', ˈmuhə̆lo 'sky'. Provisional reading: regular penultimate word stress with a small set of final-stressed (prefixed numeral) and antepenult (schwa/epenthetic-vowel) exceptions. This is my tabulation of primary data, not an author's statement.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing (Taber marks one stress per word).
new_statements.exceptions: None stated by any author; data residue listed above (final stress on vi- numerals; antepenult with post-tonic ə).
new_statements.domain_note: Citation forms of a 193-item elicited wordlist (single words, some with fossilised -o/-a endings and subject prefixes); word-level primary stress only.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources refer to the Batumerah village variety on the NW coast of Damar (Taber's 'North Damar', Chlenov's 'Damar Batumerah'; also spoken in Kuai/Kwai) = Glottolog west2548 / ISO drn; not to be confused with East Damar (Damar-Wulur, dmr, east2472) or with the extinct Batumerah language of Ambon (batu1259) that appears in Grimes & Edwards 2026.
